angles: The Execution Loop vs Single-Prompt Divide: Why the architectural choice between iterative agent loops and one-shot prompts determines everything about code quality, debugging effort, and developer satisfaction

When Loops Win and When Prompts Win: Long-running execution loops excel at refactoring, test generation, and multi-file changes while single-prompt workflows remain optimal for simple edits, boilerplate, and code explanation — understanding the threshold is the key skill

Context Management is the Hidden Engineering Challenge: How tools handle context window pressure — compaction, memory systems, and session awareness — separates production-grade execution loops from toy agents

The True Cost of Agent Loops: Token consumption in execution loops can be 5-10x higher than single prompts, but the code quality improvement and reduced debugging time often justify the cost — a framework for measuring ROI

Tool-Specific Execution Loop Architectures: How Claude Code (CLI loop + compaction), Cursor (Agent Mode + Background Agents), Windsurf (Cascade), OpenAI Codex (3-tier loop), and Gemini CLI (continuous session) each implement long-running execution differently

Failure Modes of Long-Running Agents: Step repetition, reasoning-action mismatches, tool misuse, and context decay are the four systematic failure patterns — and how Plan Mode, checkpointing, and validation loops prevent them

The Future is Hybrid: Neither pure loop nor pure single-prompt wins — the emerging pattern is Plan Mode for analysis → execution loops for implementation → single prompts for validation, all combined in a unified workflow
